//: Who the post-deploy smoke run signs in as, and the ONE library it may
reach. Loaded by scripts/prod-seed-smoke.py from studio-prod.yaml before
the smoke suite runs, idempotently, on every deploy — so a pool or a table
recreated tomorrow is restored by the next run rather than found later as
a mystery smoke failure.
EXACTLY ONE MEMBERSHIP, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The API resolves a
request's library from the caller's own membership rows: a caller with one
membership can only ever address that library, and every route then checks
the node's own `lib` against those same rows. So one membership is not a
convention this file follows — it is the mechanism that makes the smoke
account structurally unable to see, list, write or delete anything in
anyone else's library. The seeder writes this membership and no other, and
refuses to hand the account to the suite if it finds a second one; the
suite's first assertion is that GET /api/libraries returns this library
and nothing else.
NEITHER HALF OF THE IDENTITY IS COMMITTED. Both are placeholders expanded
from the environment at seed time, and the seeder refuses to run if
either resolves empty. The address was committed until it was decided
that no account address belongs in this repository: `.test` is a reserved
TLD (RFC 2606) and can never be a real mailbox, which made committing it
harmless, but it left one account described in two kinds of place. The
seeder still enforces the `.test` rule — against the value the
environment supplies, which is the half that can now be got wrong.
A default for either here would be a credential, or an identity, in the
repository. SMOKE_TEST_USER_EMAIL and SMOKE_TEST_USER_PASSWORD both come
from the studio-production environment.
THE IDS ARE FIXED, NOT GENERATED. A fresh library id per run would leave
the account holding a new membership every deploy, which breaks the one
property above within a week. They are readable rather than UUIDs so that
a row seen by hand in the table says what it is.
